name: Red Yucca
description: Drought-tolerant succulent with tall red flower spikes, attracts hummingbirds.
long_description: Red Yucca (Hesperaloe parviflora) is a drought-tolerant Texas native succulent ideal for xeriscaping, rock gardens, and low-water landscapes. Features narrow, arching green foliage forming a dense rosette and produces tall 3–5 ft flower spikes with tubular red blooms that attract hummingbirds and pollinators from spring through summer. Thrives in full sun, heat, and well-drained sandy or rocky soils, with excellent resistance to drought, poor soil conditions, and extreme temperatures. Low-maintenance perennial commonly used in desert landscapes, native plant gardens, and water-wise designs.

name: Texas Sage
description: Hardy shrub with silvery foliage and purple blooms after rain.
long_description: Texas Sage (Leucophyllum frutescens), also called Cenizo, is a drought-tolerant evergreen shrub native to Texas, widely used in xeriscaping and low-water landscapes. Known for silvery-gray foliage and vibrant purple flowers that bloom after rainfall or humidity changes. Grows 4–8 ft tall and wide, forming a dense hedge or screening plant. Thrives in full sun, heat, and well-drained soils, with high tolerance to drought, poor soils, and arid climates. Ideal for native landscapes, desert gardens, and low-maintenance hedges.

name: Mexican Plum
description: Small tree with fragrant white flowers and edible fruit.
long_description: Mexican Plum (Prunus mexicana) is a native Texas deciduous tree valued for early spring fragrant white flowers, edible summer fruit, and ornamental bark. Typically grows 15–30 ft tall, supporting pollinators with early-season blooms and providing wildlife food sources. Adapts to full sun or partial shade and performs best in well-drained soils. Suitable for native landscapes, wildlife gardens, edible gardens, and ornamental understory planting. Moderate water needs with good drought tolerance once established.

name: Desert Mallow
description: Heat-loving perennial with bright orange flowers.
long_description: Desert Mallow (Sphaeralcea ambigua) is a heat-tolerant, drought-resistant perennial suited for xeriscaping and arid Texas landscapes. Produces bright orange cup-shaped flowers from spring through fall, attracting bees and pollinators. Grows 2–4 ft tall and thrives in full sun with well-drained sandy or rocky soils. Highly tolerant of drought, poor soil conditions, and extreme heat. Ideal for native plant gardens, desert landscapes, pollinator gardens, and low-maintenance planting designs.

name: Autumn Sage
description: Compact shrub with red blooms, attracts pollinators.
long_description: Autumn Sage (Salvia greggii) is a compact, drought-tolerant Texas native shrub known for continuous red, pink, or coral blooms from spring through fall. Grows 2–4 ft tall and attracts hummingbirds, butterflies, and pollinators. Thrives in full sun and well-drained soils, tolerating heat, drought, and poor soil conditions. Commonly used in xeriscaping, pollinator gardens, borders, and container planting. Low-maintenance perennial shrub ideal for water-wise landscapes and native plant designs.

name: Lantana
description: Colorful flowering plant that thrives in heat and poor soil.
long_description: Lantana (Lantana camara) is a heat-tolerant, drought-resistant perennial widely used in Texas landscapes for continuous multicolor blooms. Produces clusters of yellow, orange, red, and pink flowers that shift in color as they mature, attracting butterflies, bees, and pollinators. Grows 1–3 ft tall with a spreading habit, thriving in full sun and well-drained soils. Highly tolerant of drought, poor soils, and extreme heat, making it ideal for xeriscaping, pollinator gardens, groundcover, and low-maintenance landscapes.

name: Prickly Pear Cactus
description: Iconic cactus with edible pads and bright blooms.
long_description: Prickly Pear Cactus (Opuntia spp.) is a drought-tolerant native cactus ideal for desert landscapes, xeriscaping, and low-water gardens. Features flat paddle-shaped pads and produces vibrant yellow to orange flowers followed by edible fruit. Thrives in full sun and extremely well-drained soils, with exceptional tolerance to drought, heat, and poor soil conditions. Provides wildlife habitat and food sources while requiring minimal maintenance, making it suitable for rock gardens, native plant landscapes, and arid environments.

name: Blackfoot Daisy
description: Low-growing perennial with white daisy-like flowers.
long_description: Blackfoot Daisy (Melampodium leucanthum) is a low-growing, drought-tolerant Texas native perennial valued for long-lasting white daisy-like flowers with yellow centers. Blooms from spring through fall, attracting pollinators such as bees and butterflies. Forms a compact mound 6–12 inches tall, thriving in full sun and well-drained rocky or sandy soils. Highly tolerant of drought, heat, and poor soils, making it ideal for xeriscaping, borders, rock gardens, and groundcover in low-maintenance landscapes.

name: Gulf Muhly
description: Ornamental grass with airy pink flower plumes.
long_description: Gulf Muhly (Muhlenbergia capillaris) is an ornamental native grass known for airy pink flower plumes that create a soft, cloud-like appearance in late summer and fall. Grows 2–4 ft tall and thrives in full sun, adapting to sandy, coastal, and well-drained soils. Requires moderate water during establishment and becomes drought tolerant over time. Commonly used in mass plantings, borders, and naturalistic landscapes for texture, seasonal color, and erosion control.

name: Turk’s Cap
description: Shade-tolerant plant with red flowers resembling a turban.
long_description: Turk’s Cap (Malvaviscus arboreus var. drummondii) is a shade-tolerant Texas native perennial known for its unique red, turban-shaped flowers that attract hummingbirds and pollinators. Grows 3–6 ft tall, forming dense foliage ideal for understory planting and shaded landscapes. Thrives in partial shade to full shade with well-drained soils and moderate water needs. Commonly used in woodland gardens, native landscapes, and pollinator-friendly designs for its tropical appearance and adaptability.

name: Bluebonnet
description: Texas state flower with vibrant blue spikes.
long_description: Bluebonnet (Lupinus texensis) is the iconic Texas state flower, valued for vibrant blue flower spikes that bloom in spring across meadows and landscapes. This sun-loving annual thrives in well-drained soils and reseeds easily, returning year after year in naturalized settings. Grows 1–2 ft tall and supports pollinators while improving soil health through nitrogen fixation. Ideal for wildflower meadows, roadside plantings, and native landscapes seeking seasonal color and ecological benefits.

name: Indian Blanket
description: Wildflower with red and yellow petals.
long_description: Indian Blanket (Gaillardia pulchella) is a drought-tolerant Texas native wildflower known for red and yellow daisy-like blooms that persist from spring through fall. Grows 1–2 ft tall and thrives in full sun with well-drained soils, tolerating heat, drought, and poor soil conditions. Highly attractive to bees, butterflies, and pollinators. Commonly used in wildflower mixes, meadows, and native landscapes for long-lasting color, resilience, and ecological value.

name: Coral Honeysuckle
description: Climbing vine with tubular red flowers.
long_description: Coral Honeysuckle (Lonicera sempervirens) is a native Texas climbing vine valued for tubular red flowers that attract hummingbirds and pollinators in spring and summer. Grows 10–20 ft with support, making it ideal for trellises, fences, and arbors. Thrives in full sun to partial shade with moderate water and adapts to various soil types. Low-maintenance and drought tolerant once established, commonly used for vertical interest in native and pollinator-friendly landscapes.

name: Esperanza
description: Shrub with bright yellow trumpet-shaped flowers.
long_description: Esperanza (Tecoma stans), also known as Yellow Bells, is a fast-growing drought-tolerant Texas shrub producing bright yellow trumpet-shaped flowers from late spring through fall. Grows 4–8 ft tall and thrives in full sun with well-drained soils. Highly tolerant of heat, drought, and poor soil conditions once established. Attracts bees, butterflies, and hummingbirds, making it ideal for xeriscaping, pollinator gardens, and low-maintenance landscapes.

name: Winecup
description: Groundcover with deep purple cup-shaped flowers.
long_description: Winecup (Callirhoe involucrata) is a low-growing Texas native groundcover known for deep purple cup-shaped flowers that bloom in spring and early summer. Forms a spreading mat 6–12 inches tall, ideal for erosion control, borders, and rock gardens. Thrives in full sun and well-drained soils, with strong drought tolerance once established. Attracts pollinators and is widely used in xeriscaping, native plant landscapes, and low-maintenance groundcover applications.

name: Flame Acanthus
description: Shrub with orange-red tubular flowers loved by hummingbirds.
long_description: Flame Acanthus (Anisacanthus quadrifidus var. wrightii) is a drought-tolerant native Texas shrub valued for hummingbird-friendly orange-red tubular flowers, summer-to-fall bloom cycles, and resilience in extreme heat. Growing 3 to 5 feet tall, it thrives in full sun and well-drained rocky or sandy soils, making it ideal for xeriscaping, pollinator gardens, and low-water landscapes. This deciduous shrub is highly attractive to hummingbirds, butterflies, and bees, providing critical nectar during late-season periods when fewer plants are blooming. It requires minimal irrigation once established, tolerates poor soils, and performs well in native plant landscapes, wildlife habitats, and water-wise garden designs focused on sustainability and biodiversity.

name: Yaupon Holly
description: Evergreen shrub with red berries and dense foliage.
long_description: Yaupon Holly (Ilex vomitoria) is a versatile native Texas evergreen shrub or small tree known for dense foliage, bright red winter berries, and adaptability across a wide range of landscape conditions. Growing 10 to 20 feet tall, it thrives in full sun to partial shade and tolerates clay, sandy, and well-drained soils, making it ideal for hedges, privacy screens, wildlife gardens, and urban landscapes. The persistent berries provide an important winter food source for birds, while the plant offers nesting habitat and year-round structure. Yaupon Holly is drought tolerant once established, responds well to pruning, and is widely used in native landscaping, restoration projects, and low-maintenance designs focused on ecological value and habitat support.

name: Cenizo
description: Also known as Texas sage, produces purple blooms after rain.
long_description: Cenizo (Leucophyllum frutescens), commonly known as Texas Sage, is a drought-tolerant evergreen shrub native to arid Texas regions, recognized for silvery-gray foliage and purple blooms triggered by humidity and rainfall. Growing 4 to 8 feet tall and wide, it thrives in full sun and sharply drained soils, especially limestone, sandy, or rocky conditions common in xeriscapes. This low-water shrub is highly heat tolerant and requires minimal irrigation, making it a staple for drought-resistant landscaping, native plant gardens, and desert-style designs. Cenizo provides seasonal color, structural form, and pollinator value while resisting deer and tolerating poor soils, making it ideal for sustainable, low-maintenance landscapes.

name: Gregg’s Mistflower
description: Perennial with soft purple-blue flowers attracting butterflies.
long_description: Gregg’s Mistflower (Conoclinium greggii) is a native Texas perennial known for clusters of soft purple-blue flowers that bloom late summer through fall, providing critical nectar for butterflies, especially monarchs. Growing 1 to 3 feet tall and spreading readily, it thrives in full sun with moderate water and adapts to a variety of soils, including clay and limestone. This pollinator plant is ideal for butterfly gardens, native landscapes, and naturalized areas where seasonal color and ecological support are priorities. Gregg’s Mistflower is valued for extending bloom periods into late season, supporting migration cycles, and enhancing biodiversity in wildlife-friendly and sustainable garden designs.

name: Texas Redbud
description: Small tree with bright pink spring blooms.
long_description: Texas Redbud (Cercis canadensis var. texensis) is a native ornamental tree prized for vivid pink to magenta spring flowers that bloom before leaf emergence, creating strong seasonal visual impact. Growing 15 to 25 feet tall, it thrives in partial shade to full sun and well-drained soils, including rocky limestone soils common in Central Texas. This drought-tolerant tree is widely used as an understory tree, accent plant, or focal point in native and residential landscapes. It supports early-season pollinators, provides moderate shade, and offers heart-shaped foliage that enhances visual interest, making it ideal for sustainable landscaping and habitat-focused garden design.

name: Buttonbush
description: Water-loving shrub with spherical white flowers.
long_description: Buttonbush (Cephalanthus occidentalis) is a native Texas wetland shrub known for its distinctive spherical white flower clusters and strong ecological value in aquatic and riparian environments. Growing 6 to 12 feet tall, it thrives in full sun to partial shade and prefers consistently moist to wet soils, including standing water, making it ideal for rain gardens, pond edges, and flood-prone landscapes. Its nectar-rich blooms attract bees, butterflies, and other pollinators, while its structure provides habitat for birds and wildlife. Buttonbush is widely used in habitat restoration, erosion control, and water management projects, offering both ornamental interest and functional environmental benefits.

name: Bald Cypress
description: Large deciduous tree tolerant of wet soils.
long_description: Bald Cypress (Taxodium distichum) is a long-lived native Texas tree adapted to floodplains and wetland environments, recognized for feathery foliage, buttressed trunks, and tolerance of standing water. Growing 50 to 100 feet tall, it thrives in full sun and high-moisture soils, including periodically flooded areas, making it ideal for large landscapes, parks, and ecological restoration projects. This tree provides critical habitat for birds and wildlife, supports aquatic ecosystems, and contributes to erosion control and water stabilization. Its golden fall foliage adds seasonal interest, while its resilience makes it a cornerstone species for sustainable, climate-adaptive landscape design.

name: Inland Sea Oats
description: Shade-tolerant ornamental grass.
long_description: Inland Sea Oats (Chasmanthium latifolium) is a native ornamental grass valued for its shade tolerance and distinctive oat-like seed heads that provide texture and movement in the landscape. Growing 2 to 4 feet tall, it thrives in partial shade to full shade and prefers moist, well-drained soils, making it ideal for woodland gardens, shaded borders, and erosion control on slopes. The drooping seed heads persist into fall and winter, offering visual interest and food for birds. This grass is widely used in native plantings and naturalized landscapes for its adaptability, ecological benefits, and ability to thrive in low-light conditions.

name: Swamp Milkweed
description: Milkweed species that prefers moist soils.
long_description: Swamp Milkweed (Asclepias incarnata) is a native perennial essential for pollinator and monarch butterfly habitats, producing clusters of pink flowers rich in nectar during summer. Growing 3 to 5 feet tall, it thrives in full sun to partial shade and prefers moist to wet soils, making it ideal for rain gardens, pond margins, and low-lying landscape areas. As a host plant for monarch caterpillars, it plays a critical role in supporting butterfly life cycles and biodiversity. This plant is widely used in ecological restoration, pollinator gardens, and sustainable landscapes focused on habitat creation and water management.

name: American Beautyberry
description: Shrub with bright purple berries.
long_description: American Beautyberry (Callicarpa americana) is a native Texas deciduous shrub known for its striking clusters of bright purple berries that provide strong seasonal interest and wildlife value. Growing 3 to 6 feet tall, it thrives in partial shade and moist, well-drained soils, making it ideal for woodland gardens, understory plantings, and native landscapes. The berries serve as an important food source for birds and small mammals, while the plant supports biodiversity in habitat-focused designs. Beautyberry is valued for its ornamental appeal, adaptability, and role in sustainable landscaping that prioritizes ecological function and native species.

name: Texas Star Hibiscus
description: Showy red hibiscus for wet areas.
long_description: Texas Star Hibiscus (Hibiscus coccineus) is a bold native perennial adapted to wet environments, known for large star-shaped red flowers that attract hummingbirds and pollinators throughout summer. Growing 4 to 6 feet tall, it thrives in full sun and consistently moist to saturated soils, making it ideal for rain gardens, pond edges, and water features. This plant provides strong vertical interest, vibrant color, and ecological value in aquatic or high-moisture landscapes. It is widely used in pollinator gardens and native plant designs focused on biodiversity, water management, and habitat support.

name: Anacacho Orchid Tree
description: Small ornamental tree with orchid-like flowers.
long_description: Anacacho Orchid Tree (Bauhinia lunarioides) is a small native Texas tree valued for its delicate white to pale pink orchid-like flowers and drought tolerance in rocky soils. Growing 10 to 20 feet tall, it thrives in full sun and well-drained limestone or sandy soils, making it ideal for xeriscaping and water-wise landscapes. This ornamental tree provides seasonal spring blooms, light canopy shade, and visual interest in compact spaces. It is commonly used as an accent tree in native landscapes and low-maintenance garden designs that prioritize resilience and reduced irrigation.

name: Pickerelweed
description: Aquatic plant with purple spikes.
long_description: Pickerelweed (Pontederia cordata) is a native aquatic perennial adapted to shallow water environments, producing upright spikes of purple flowers above glossy green foliage. It thrives in full sun and standing water, making it ideal for ponds, wetlands, and water gardens. This plant provides habitat for aquatic wildlife and supports pollinators, contributing to healthy freshwater ecosystems. Pickerelweed is widely used in ecological restoration, shoreline stabilization, and naturalized aquatic plantings for its environmental benefits and ornamental appeal.

name: Cedar Elm
description: Hardy native shade tree.
long_description: Cedar Elm (Ulmus crassifolia) is a durable native Texas shade tree known for its adaptability, moderate drought tolerance, and strong performance in urban and suburban landscapes. Growing 40 to 70 feet tall, it thrives in full sun and a wide range of soils, including clay, limestone, and sandy conditions. This tree provides dense shade, supports wildlife, and is resistant to many environmental stresses, making it ideal for streetscapes, residential yards, and large landscape plantings. Its resilience and low maintenance requirements make it a reliable choice for sustainable landscape design.

name: Scarlet Sage
description: Bright red flowering perennial.
long_description: Scarlet Sage (Salvia coccinea) is a native Texas perennial known for its vivid red flowers and long blooming season from spring through fall, making it highly attractive to hummingbirds, butterflies, and pollinators. Growing 1 to 3 feet tall, it thrives in full sun to partial shade with moderate water and adapts to a variety of soil types. This plant is ideal for pollinator gardens, borders, and native landscapes, providing continuous color and ecological value. Scarlet Sage is easy to grow, reseeds readily, and supports biodiversity in sustainable, wildlife-friendly garden designs.

name: Possumhaw Holly
description: Deciduous holly with bright red berries.
long_description: Possumhaw Holly (Ilex decidua) is a native Texas deciduous shrub or small tree valued for its bright red berries that persist through winter, providing strong seasonal interest and wildlife support. Growing 10 to 20 feet tall, it thrives in full sun to partial shade and prefers moist, well-drained soils, adapting well to floodplain and lowland conditions. The berries serve as an important winter food source for birds, while the plant offers habitat and structure in native landscapes. Possumhaw Holly is widely used in habitat restoration, naturalized plantings, and sustainable landscape designs focused on biodiversity and seasonal visual impact.

name: Switchgrass
description: Tall native prairie grass.
long_description: Switchgrass (Panicum virgatum) is a native warm-season prairie grass valued for its height, adaptability, and ecological benefits in Texas landscapes. Growing 3 to 6 feet tall, it thrives in full sun and tolerates a wide range of soil conditions, from dry uplands to moderately moist sites. This grass is widely used for erosion control, habitat restoration, and sustainable landscaping due to its deep root system and ability to improve soil structure. Its airy seed heads provide seasonal texture and movement, while also supporting birds and wildlife in native and naturalized plantings.

name: Texas Persimmon
description: Small tree with edible fruit.
long_description: Texas Persimmon (Diospyros texana) is a native small tree known for its smooth gray bark, drought tolerance, and sweet edible black fruit that supports both wildlife and human use. Growing 10 to 20 feet tall, it thrives in full sun and well-drained soils, particularly limestone and rocky conditions common in Central Texas. This tree is highly drought tolerant once established and is widely used in xeriscaping, native landscapes, and low-water garden designs. It provides food for birds and mammals while adding ornamental value through its bark, foliage, and seasonal fruit production.

name: Turk’s Cap Hibiscus
description: Tropical-looking native perennial.
long_description: Turk’s Cap Hibiscus (Malvaviscus arboreus var. drummondii) is a shade-tolerant native Texas perennial known for its bright red, turban-shaped flowers and lush, tropical appearance. Growing 3 to 6 feet tall, it thrives in partial shade with moderate to high water and performs well in woodland gardens and understory plantings. This plant is highly attractive to hummingbirds and butterflies, providing consistent nectar sources throughout the growing season. It is widely used in native landscaping, pollinator gardens, and shaded environments where low-maintenance, wildlife-friendly plants are needed.

name: Little Bluestem
description: Native ornamental grass with fall color.
long_description: Little Bluestem (Schizachyrium scoparium) is a native warm-season grass prized for its blue-green foliage that transitions to coppery-orange hues in fall, adding strong seasonal interest. Growing 2 to 4 feet tall, it thrives in full sun and well-drained soils with low water requirements once established. This grass is ideal for prairie plantings, erosion control, and low-maintenance landscapes, supporting pollinators and providing habitat for wildlife. Its drought tolerance and adaptability make it a key species in sustainable, native, and xeriscape garden designs.

name: Mayhaw
description: Small tree producing edible berries.
long_description: Mayhaw (Crataegus opaca) is a native Texas wetland tree known for its tart red berries commonly used in jellies and preserves, as well as its ecological value in floodplain environments. Growing 15 to 30 feet tall, it thrives in full sun and high-moisture soils, including areas prone to seasonal flooding. This tree supports wildlife by providing food for birds and mammals while also contributing to habitat diversity in wetland ecosystems. Mayhaw is widely used in native landscapes, edible gardens, and restoration projects focused on water management, biodiversity, and sustainable land use.

name: Frogfruit
description: Low-growing groundcover for moist areas.
long_description: Frogfruit (Phyla nodiflora) is a low-growing native groundcover valued for its ability to form dense mats and support pollinators in Texas landscapes. It thrives in full sun to partial shade and tolerates a range of soil moisture conditions from moderate to periodically wet, making it ideal for erosion control, lawn alternatives, and naturalized plantings. This plant produces small white to pale purple flowers that attract butterflies and bees, contributing to biodiversity and habitat support. Frogfruit is widely used in sustainable landscaping for its resilience, low maintenance needs, and effectiveness in stabilizing soil.

name: Texas Mountain Laurel
description: Evergreen shrub with fragrant purple flowers.
long_description: Texas Mountain Laurel (Sophora secundiflora) is a native evergreen shrub or small tree prized for its glossy foliage and highly fragrant purple flower clusters that bloom in spring. Growing 10 to 20 feet tall, it thrives in full sun and well-drained soils, particularly limestone-rich conditions, and requires low water once established. This drought-tolerant plant is widely used in xeriscaping, native landscapes, and ornamental garden designs for its fragrance, structure, and resilience. It also supports pollinators and adds year-round visual interest, making it a key species in sustainable, low-maintenance landscapes.

name: Golden Groundsel
description: Early spring bloomer for moist shade.
long_description: Golden Groundsel (Packera obovata) is a native perennial groundcover known for its bright yellow flowers that bloom in early spring and provide early-season nectar for pollinators. It thrives in partial shade with moist, well-drained soils, making it ideal for woodland gardens, shaded borders, and rain gardens. Growing low and spreading, it forms dense colonies that help suppress weeds and stabilize soil. This plant is widely used in native landscaping and ecological restoration for its adaptability, seasonal color, and role in supporting pollinator populations.

name: Pecan Tree
description: Large native tree producing edible nuts.
long_description: Pecan Tree (Carya illinoinensis) is a large native Texas tree valued for its edible nuts, extensive shade canopy, and ecological importance in riparian and agricultural landscapes. Growing 70 to 100 feet tall, it thrives in full sun and deep, well-drained soils with moderate to high water availability. This long-lived tree supports wildlife by providing food and habitat, while also offering economic value through nut production. Pecan trees are widely used in orchards, large landscapes, and sustainable land management systems that integrate food production, shade, and biodiversity.

name: Twistleaf Yucca
description: Compact yucca with curly leaves.
long_description: Twistleaf Yucca (Yucca rupicola) is a drought-tolerant native Texas succulent known for its narrow, twisting leaves and tall flower spikes bearing creamy white blooms. Growing in compact rosettes with flower stalks reaching several feet tall, it thrives in full sun and well-drained rocky or sandy soils, making it ideal for xeriscaping, rock gardens, and low-water landscapes. This plant is highly heat tolerant and requires minimal irrigation once established, providing strong architectural form and year-round interest. It also supports pollinators such as moths and bees, contributing to biodiversity in native and sustainable garden designs.

name: Resurrection Fern
description: Fern that revives after drying out.
long_description: Resurrection Fern (Pleopeltis polypodioides) is a unique native epiphytic fern capable of surviving extreme dehydration and rapidly rehydrating after rainfall. It grows on tree trunks, rocks, and other surfaces in shaded, humid environments, thriving in full shade with moderate moisture. This plant is well-suited for woodland gardens, shaded landscapes, and naturalized settings where it adds ecological interest and texture. Its drought survival adaptation makes it a notable species for resilience-focused landscaping and educational or conservation-oriented plantings.

name: Southern Wood Fern
description: Shade-loving native fern.
long_description: Southern Wood Fern (Thelypteris kunthii) is a hardy native fern that thrives in shaded, moisture-rich environments, forming dense clumps of arching green fronds. Growing 2 to 4 feet tall, it performs best in full shade with consistently moist soils, making it ideal for woodland gardens, shaded borders, and understory plantings. This fern adds soft texture and lush greenery to landscapes while contributing to soil health and moisture retention. It is commonly used in native landscaping and ecological restoration projects focused on shade-tolerant plant communities.

name: Purple Coneflower
description: Popular native wildflower with purple petals.
long_description: Purple Coneflower (Echinacea purpurea) is a native Texas wildflower known for its large purple blooms with prominent central cones, providing long-lasting color and strong pollinator support. Growing 2 to 4 feet tall, it thrives in full sun with low to moderate water and adapts to a variety of well-drained soils. This plant attracts bees, butterflies, and birds, making it a cornerstone species in pollinator gardens, prairie plantings, and native landscapes. Its drought tolerance, reseeding ability, and ecological benefits make it ideal for sustainable and low-maintenance garden designs.

name: Spiderwort
description: Shade-tolerant wildflower with blue blooms.
long_description: Spiderwort (Tradescantia spp.) is a native Texas wildflower valued for its blue to purple flowers and ability to thrive in shaded to partially shaded environments. Growing 1 to 3 feet tall, it prefers moist, well-drained soils and is commonly used in woodland gardens, shaded borders, and native plantings. Its blooms open in the morning and attract pollinators such as bees, contributing to ecological diversity. Spiderwort is appreciated for its adaptability, low maintenance requirements, and role in supporting pollinator-friendly and sustainable landscapes.

name: Sideoats Grama
description: Native prairie grass with dangling seeds.
long_description: Sideoats Grama (Bouteloua curtipendula) is a native Texas prairie grass recognized for its distinctive one-sided oat-like seed spikes and strong drought tolerance. Growing 2 to 3 feet tall, it thrives in full sun and well-drained soils including rocky, sandy, and clay conditions, making it ideal for xeriscaping, prairie restoration, and erosion control. This warm-season grass requires minimal water once established and provides habitat and forage for wildlife. It is widely used in native landscapes, meadow plantings, and sustainable landscaping for its resilience, soil stabilization benefits, and natural texture.

name: River Oats
description: Shade-tolerant ornamental grass.
long_description: River Oats (Chasmanthium latifolium) is a native Texas ornamental grass valued for its flat, drooping seed heads and strong shade tolerance. Growing 2 to 4 feet tall, it performs well in partial to full shade and prefers moist, well-drained soils, making it ideal for woodland gardens, shaded borders, and erosion control. This grass provides seasonal interest and supports birds and wildlife while stabilizing soil in shaded environments. It is commonly used in native plantings and naturalized landscapes for its adaptability and ecological benefits.

name: Lipstick Echeveria
description: Rosette succulent with red edges.
long_description: Lipstick Echeveria (Echeveria agavoides) is a compact rosette-forming succulent known for its green leaves edged in bright red, commonly used in xeriscaping and container gardening. It thrives in full sun and well-drained soils, requiring low water and tolerating heat and drought conditions. Typically grown in pots, rock gardens, and succulent arrangements, it provides strong visual contrast and architectural form. This low-maintenance plant is well suited for water-wise landscapes and modern garden designs.
